found.summary:
I checked these on 2026-10-23. Stock comes from data embedded in each page: Tsoft PRODUCT_DATA quantity, schema.org JSON-LD availability, and the ikas "Stok: N" field. For robotistan, direnc, robotsepeti, motorobit, robolinkmarket, samm, robocombo, f1depo, elektrovadi, robotzade, komponentci, robitshop, hobidunya and ozdisan I also went through the full product sitemaps, so nothing should be missing for those shops.

**Main result: there is no Feetech STS3215 / Waveshare ST3215 in stock anywhere in Turkey that I could check.**
- All 5 ST3215 listings are out of stock: direnc 12V 30kg and ST3215-HS, Samm 7.4V and 12V, robotsepeti 12V.
- ST3020 is out of stock at direnc and Samm.
- The Feetech-branded STS3215, STS3032, STS3020, SCS0009, SCS15 and SM series are not listed at all.
- Hiwonder/LewanSoul bus servos (LX-16A, LX-224, LX-225, HX-35HM, HTS-35H, HTD-45H), Kondo, DSServo bus servos and Waveshare SC09 are not listed in any Turkish shop. UBTECH appears only as kits, without prices.
- DYNAMIXEL XL330-M288-T, XL330-M077-T, XL430-W250-T, XC330, XL-320 and single AX-12A are out of stock at robotsepeti, the ROBOTIS dealer.

**Bus servos that are in stock:**
- Samm: Waveshare SC15, 10 units, 1,318.85 TL. This is the cheapest in-stock bus servo, but it uses a potentiometer (1024 steps over 210°) and the SCS protocol.
- Samm: Waveshare ST3025, 44 units, 6,564.41 TL each. 12V, 40 kg·cm, steel gears, 12-bit encoder.
- Samm: Waveshare RSBL45 (RS485, 24V), 3 units, 8,295 TL.
- robotsepeti DYNAMIXEL, all very expensive:
  - AX-12A 6-pack: 1 pack, 27,765 TL, which is about 4,627 TL per servo.
  - MX-28T: 26,759 TL. The page shows 997 units, which looks like supplier stock rather than units on the shelf.
  - XM430-W350-T: 2 units, 27,765 TL.

**Adapters and controllers that are in stock:**
- Samm: Waveshare Bus Servo Adapter (A), 18 units, 328.22 TL. This is the cheapest option.
- robocombo: Waveshare Bus Servo Driver HAT (A) with ESP32, "Stok:18", 1,255 TL.
- Samm: the same HAT, 1 unit, 1,223.37 TL.
- robotsepeti: U2D2 (5 units, 3,555.52 TL), U2D2 Power Hub Board (3 units, 2,051.76 TL), OpenRB-150 (10 units, 2,438.21 TL) and DYNAMIXEL Communication Bridge (4 units, 1,612.88 TL).
- No Feetech FE-URT-1 or Hiwonder bus-servo board is listed in any Turkish shop.

**What this means for a 15-DOF duck from Turkish stock today:**
- Option 1 is 10× SC15 (about 13.2k TL) plus 5× ST3025 (about 32.8k TL). This needs two buses and two adapters, because Waveshare says not to mix ST and SC servos on one board (different protocol and voltage).
- Option 2 is to wait for Samm or direnc to restock ST3215 at about 1,595–1,690 TL each.
- Analog-feedback PWM servos are in stock if that route is wanted: Feetech FS90-FB at robotistan (23 units, 358 TL) and FT5335M-FB (16 units, 2,065 TL).

**What I could not verify:**
- Trendyol, Hepsiburada, n11, cimri, ciceksepeti, digikey.com.tr and mouser.com.tr all returned 403 or a bot check, and the Chrome extension was not connected. Their stock is unverified.
- Akakce does index Hepsiburada and n11, and it showed no ST3215 or STS3215 listings. It did show one listing for "Waveshare Serial Bus Servo Sürücü Kontrol Kartı" at 2,019.43 TL.
- Mouser's other regional sites show DFRobot SER0069 (the ST3215 7.4V) at about €20 with roughly 31 units, as an import. Stock for Turkey is unknown.

- MG90S: 0.22 (claimed; clones are often weaker)
- ES08MA II / ES08MD II: 0.20
For a robot the size of Open Duck Mini, DS3218MG (2.1 N.m @6.8 V, 60 g, 3 µs deadband) or TD-8120MG (2.1 N.m @6 V) match the STS3215's torque, but they have no position feedback.

NOT FOUND IN TURKISH STOCK: MG92B, Corona DS929MG/DS939MG, JX PDI-1109/1181/4409, KST and Savox micros, EMAX ES3352, Feetech FT5313M-FB, DS3218 270°/feedback versions. These are import-only.

QUALITY PROBLEMS: Turkish shops say this on their own product pages:
- Robotistan and SAMM: on their MG90S only the last gear stage is metal and the inner gears are plastic. Robotistan says the same of its MG996R.
- Komponentci: gear material in SG90, MG90S and MG945 changes from batch to batch.
- Robolink: labels its MG90S, MG995 and MG996R as "KLON". F1Depo labels an S3003 as a clone.
The Vorpal wiki reports these problems with counterfeit MG90S:
- 10-15 % of gearboxes are bad out of the box
- 2-90° drift as the servo warms up
- chatter under load
- less than half the rated torque
A Tuya forum teardown found the motor gear and inner gears were plastic.
An SG90 test with default pulse limits was off by up to about 15°. Setting min/max to 600/2320 µs fixed most of it. So each servo needs its own calibration, and buying spares makes sense.
None of these servos lists a backlash figure. The Microduck work models ±1° of play even for XL330s.

PCA9685 NOTES:
- At 50 Hz each step is about 4.9 µs (about 0.44° per count), which is coarser than the 1-3 µs deadband of good digital servos. Raising the PWM frequency to around 200-330 Hz for digital servos gives finer steps.
- The internal oscillator runs at roughly 23-27 MHz, so each board needs calibrating.
- Servos need a separate 5-6 V supply. An MG996R stalls at 2.5 A each.

F1Depo had almost everything out of stock except Feetech FT5320M/FT5330M. Direnc's MG90S, SG90, MG996 and its cheap PCA9685 were out of stock.
